chapter_theme: Five units headed உயர் ஞானம் and தனி ஞானம் (higher and separate knowledge), addressed to Pulastya: a practice of drawing the life-letter upward in every act of the body, which makes one live to the end of the earth beyond Death's hand; the one Supreme beyond the crown and beyond Uma and Ganapati, which is one's own life as Siva; bindu, nada and the root from which the two came, whose knower becomes guru; and the siddha as the one who, having known the root, burns the shastras.
structure_note: 2415 and 2416 are the two halves of one eight-line எண்சீர் விருத்தம் split across two units; 2417 to 2419 are three full stanzas under தனி ஞானம், chaining by antadi (ஞானம் முற்றே / விந்து; மூலம் பாரே / மூலமதை). The disciple addressed is புலத்தியன், Pulastya, named in 2418 and 2419.

2415.reading: When you eat, draw the life-letter upward, and when you sleep let it all become that; whenever the organ lets go toward a woman, guard it, turn it to the right and upward, and stand in that state.
2415.nuance: உயிரெழுத்து, the life-letter, is the vowel in grammar and, in the cipher, the breath or the seed-syllable; tradition takes 'drawing it upward' as raising the breath or the semen. The third and fourth lines prescribe retention and upward turning at the moment of emission, a practice the Tirumanthiram also teaches. பேணிவலம் (guarding, to the right) and அவத்தில் (in that state, or in the avastha) are compressed and the exact instruction is unclear.

2416.reading: Food, fruit, leaf and medicine all become that very thing; those who can direct it so every day will live as long as the earth endures, and will not be caught in Death's hand.
2416.nuance: The claim is the Siddhars' kaya-siddhi: a body kept beyond death by the daily practice begun in 2415, of which this is the second half. மதுவே யாகும் (becomes that) makes whatever is eaten feed the practice rather than the body; a plain reading is that food and medicine become nectar. The verse states the claim; it does not describe a preparation.

2417.reading: Standing beyond the one space at the crown, with Uma and Ganapati left behind, the sky-light that is Om, 'a' and 'u', the ordained Supreme, is beyond anyone's reach; your own tuneful life has become Siva, and he who lay on the milk sea has become Vishnu; if you see Ganapati who is the eye with your eye, mingling and melting you will dance: knowledge is complete.
2417.nuance: The sense turns on the letters: அவ்வும் உவ்வும், 'a' and 'u', are two of the three letters of Om, and tradition reads them as Siva and Shakti, or as the sun and moon breaths. The verse first sets the Supreme beyond Uma and Ganapati and then says one's own life is Siva and Vishnu, so the gods are inner states; உந்தி (navel) may also be read for முந்தி, placing Uma and Ganapati at the navel centre.

2418.reading: If you know the standing of bindu and see its wonder, the many-voiced nada becomes the guru; if that nada with an end becomes the guru, you yourself become the guru who is beginning and end; there is no doubt, Pulastya, and all the arts and knowledges are not equal to this; if you do not know the root where the two joined on the day before, look to the root.
2418.nuance: விந்து and நாதம் are the cosmological pair (bindu and nada, the first stirrings of manifestation) and, in the body, semen and sound; the verse's claim that the knower of them becomes his own guru is clear on either reading. முந்தாநாள் இருவருமே கூடிச் சேர்ந்த மூலம், the root where the two joined, is Siva and Shakti, or father and mother at conception (as in 2409); the two readings are the same in the Siddhars' logic.

2419.reading: When the root is known, it is yoga; when it is seen in due order, it is alchemy; before the one who has seen it with skill they stand subdued; he who burns and throws away the shastras is the siddha; virtuous Pulastya, supreme yogi, if you find the salt without erring from the spoken word, and fix the knowing engine that is the light itself, it grants all siddhis: complete.
2419.nuance: வாதம் is alchemy (இரசவாதம்), so the one root yields yoga and alchemy as two orders of the same knowledge. உப்பு, salt, is a cipher word: tradition takes it as the fixed mercury or the body's own substance, and the verse gives no key. எந்திரம் (engine, yantra) for the light is unusual. The burning of the shastras is the run's sharpest claim and conflicts with 2406's command to study them.

links.note: Tirumular says that with the two breaths set in the upper palate there is no Death and grey hair and wrinkles reverse; Agasthiyar says those who direct the life-letter upward every day live as long as the earth and escape Death's hand. The same claim of bodily deathlessness by breath practice.

The Naladiyar says no one has leapt clear of Death and escaped, so give while you can; Agasthiyar says the daily practitioner lives as long as the earth and is not caught in Death's hand. The conflict holds if Agasthiyar's claim is about the physical body, as the Siddhars' kaya-siddhi tradition takes it; if 'not caught by Death' means release from rebirth, the two need not clash.

Sivavakkiyar's mantra that rose as 'a' and 'u', settled as 'a', 'u' and 'm' in the Supreme, is Sivayam; Agasthiyar's sky-light is Om, 'a' and 'u', beyond anyone's reach, and one's life is Siva. Both read the letters of Om as the inner Siva; Sivavakkiyar says the knower has no further birth, Agasthiyar that knowledge is complete.

Tirumular drives bindu and nada upward to drink the nectar, and bindu itself dies; Agasthiyar makes knowing bindu's standing turn nada into the guru and the knower into his own guru. Agasthiyar takes the pair Tirumular uses as a practice and turns it into a doctrine of the inner guru.

Pattirakiriyar asks when he will burn the shastras, make the four Vedas a lie and see the sutra; Agasthiyar says he who burns and throws away the shastras is the siddha. Both make the burning of scripture the mark of the knower rather than a loss.

2406 tells the children to look again and again at the many Vedas and shastras; 2419 says the one who burns the shastras is the siddha. Within the same work the two are incompatible unless 2406 is read ironically (its 'path made for them to live' being the livelihood path 2407 mocks) or as a stage that 2419 leaves behind.

source_issues: 2415 and 2416 are the two halves of a single eight-line எண்சீர் விருத்தம் (the rhyme runs உண்ணும் / பெண்ணின் / திண்ணும் / மண்ணூழி) printed as two four-line units; 2415 ends in a semicolon mid-stanza.
2417 line 3 runs அம்பரம்ஓம் together without a space, and the heading changes from உயர் ஞானம் to தனி ஞானம் within the run without a new காப்பு.
